{
  "claims": [
    {
      "anchor": "The SQL standard defines four isolation levels",
      "claim_text": "The SQL standard defines four isolation levels.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P0.S0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Serializable, the strictest, guarantees that concurrent serializable transactions have the same effect as running them one at a time in some order",
      "claim_text": "Serializable is the strictest isolation level.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S1", "rel": "entails", "sub": "The most strict is Serializable"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P0.S1 states Serializable is most strict."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Serializable, the strictest, guarantees that concurrent serializable transactions have the same effect as running them one at a time in some order",
      "claim_text": "Serializable guarantees that concurrent serializable transactions have the same effect as running them one at a time in some order.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P0.S1."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "PostgreSQL accepts all four",
      "claim_text": "PostgreSQL accepts all four standard isolation levels.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "you can request any of the four standard transaction isolation levels"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P1.S0 says any of four can be requested."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "implements only three",
      "claim_text": "PostgreSQL implements only three distinct isolation levels.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "internally only three distinct isolation levels are implemented"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P1.S0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "because Read Uncommitted behaves like Read Committed",
      "claim_text": "Read Uncommitted behaves like Read Committed in PostgreSQL.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "PostgreSQL's Read Uncommitted mode behaves like Read Committed"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P1.S0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Read Committed is the default",
      "claim_text": "Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P2.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P2.S0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "a SELECT sees a snapshot taken when the query starts",
      "claim_text": "At Read Committed, a SELECT sees a snapshot taken when the query starts.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P2.S2", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P2.S2 states snapshot as of query start."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "two SELECTs in the same transaction can return different data",
      "claim_text": "At Read Committed, two SELECTs in the same transaction can return different data.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P2.S4", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P2.S4 states successive SELECTs can see different data."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Repeatable Read instead takes its snapshot at the first non-transaction-control statement",
      "claim_text": "Repeatable Read takes its snapshot at the first non-transaction-control statement in the transaction.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P4.S0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "successive SELECTs in a transaction see the same data",
      "claim_text": "At Repeatable Read, successive SELECTs in a transaction see the same data.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P4.S1."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Anyone running PostgreSQL 9.0 who requested Serializable actually got the behaviour that Repeatable Read provides today",
      "claim_text": "Prior to PostgreSQL 9.1, requesting Serializable provided the same behavior as Repeatable Read today.",
      "kind": "logic",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [
        {"sid": "P5.S0", "rel": "entails"},
        {"sid": "P5.S1", "rel": "entails"}
      ],
      "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "9.0", "op": "<", "right": "9.1"},
      "reasoning": "P5.S0 says prior to 9.1 Serializable matched current Repeatable Read; 9.0 is prior to 9.1."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "a serial order would have given the second transaction a sum of 330 instead of 300",
      "claim_text": "In the class example, a serial order would have given the second transaction a sum of 330 instead of 300.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P7.S0 states B would have computed 330, not 300."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "a difference of 30",
      "claim_text": "The difference between 330 and 300 is 30.",
      "kind": "arith",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": {"kind": "arith", "expr": "330 - 300", "op": "==", "value": "30"},
      "reasoning": "Arithmetic from numbers in P7.S0."
    }
  ]
}
